title: 10. NLP, Transformers & LLMs: Complete Transformer Architecture
summary: Goal: Understand the full transformer: encoder, decoder, and all components.

sections.title: The Original Transformer (2017)
sections.body:
**Goal**: Understand the full transformer: encoder, decoder, and all components.

### "Attention Is All You Need" - Vaswani et al.

**Task**: Machine Translation (English → French)

```
Input:  "The cat sat on the mat"
Output: "Le chat était assis sur le tapis"

Architecture: Encoder-Decoder
```

sections.title: High-Level Architecture
sections.body:
```
ENCODER (left side)              DECODER (right side)
────────────                     ────────────

Input: "The cat sat"             Output (shifted): "<start> Le chat"

↓ Word Embeddings                ↓ Word Embeddings
↓ + Positional Encoding          ↓ + Positional Encoding
↓                                ↓
┌──────────────────┐            ┌──────────────────┐
│ Encoder Layer 1  │            │ Decoder Layer 1  │
│ • Self-Attention │            │ • Masked Self-Attention
│ • Feed Forward   │            │ • Cross-Attention (to encoder)
└──────────────────┘            │ • Feed Forward   │
↓                                └──────────────────┘
┌──────────────────┐            ↓
│ Encoder Layer 2  │            ┌──────────────────┐
│ (same structure) │            │ Decoder Layer 2  │
└──────────────────┘            │ (same structure) │
↓                                └──────────────────┘
... (N=6 layers)                 ↓
↓                                ... (N=6 layers)
Encoder Output                   ↓
        ↓                        ↓ Linear + Softmax
        └────────────────────────→ Probabilities
                                 ↓
                                "Le chat était ..."
```

sections.title: Components Breakdown
sections.body:
### 1. Input Embedding + Positional Encoding

```python
# Convert words to vectors
word_emb = embedding_layer(tokens)        # (batch, seq_len, d_model)

# Add position information
pos_enc = positional_encoding(seq_len)    # (seq_len, d_model)
input_emb = word_emb + pos_enc           # (batch, seq_len, d_model)
```

### 2. Encoder Layer (repeated N times)

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
│  INPUT                              │
│    ↓                                │
│  Multi-Head Self-Attention          │
│    ↓                                │
│  Add & Norm (Residual + LayerNorm)  │
│    ↓                                │
│  Feed-Forward Network               │
│    ↓                                │
│  Add & Norm (Residual + LayerNorm)  │
│    ↓                                │
│  OUTPUT                             │
└─────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### 3. Decoder Layer (repeated N times)

```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  INPUT (from previous decoder layer)     │
│    ↓                                     │
│  Masked Multi-Head Self-Attention        │
│    ↓                                     │
│  Add & Norm                              │
│    ↓                                     │
│  Multi-Head Cross-Attention              │
│  (attends to encoder output)             │
│    ↓                                     │
│  Add & Norm                              │
│    ↓                                     │
│  Feed-Forward Network                    │
│    ↓                                     │
│  Add & Norm                              │
│    ↓                                     │
│  OUTPUT                                  │
└──────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

sections.title: Key Components Explained
sections.body:
### Multi-Head Attention
```
• Multiple attention heads (8 in original)
• Each head learns different patterns
• Outputs concatenated and projected
```

### Feed-Forward Network
```python
FFN(x) = ReLU(xW₁ + b₁)W₂ + b₂

# Two linear layers with ReLU
# Applied independently to each position
# Same network for all positions

Dimensions:
  Input:  d_model = 512
  Hidden: d_ff = 2048 (4× expansion)
  Output: d_model = 512
```

### Layer Normalization
```python
LayerNorm(x) = γ × (x - μ) / (σ + ε) + β

# Normalizes across features (not batch)
# Stabilizes training
# γ, β are learned parameters
```

### Residual Connections
```python
output = LayerNorm(x + Sublayer(x))

# Skip connections help gradient flow
# Enable training very deep networks
```

sections.title: PyTorch Implementation
sections.body:
### Encoder Layer:

```python
class EncoderLayer(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, d_model, num_heads, d_ff, dropout=0.1):
        super().__init__()
        
        # Multi-head self-attention
        self.self_attn = MultiHeadAttention(d_model, num_heads)
        
        # Feed-forward network
        self.ffn = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(d_model, d_ff),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Dropout(dropout),
            nn.Linear(d_ff, d_model)
        )
        
        # Layer normalization
        self.norm1 = nn.LayerNorm(d_model)
        self.norm2 = nn.LayerNorm(d_model)
        
        # Dropout
        self.dropout1 = nn.Dropout(dropout)
        self.dropout2 = nn.Dropout(dropout)
    
    def forward(self, x, mask=None):
        # Self-attention with residual
        attn_output, _ = self.self_attn(x, x, x, mask)
        x = self.norm1(x + self.dropout1(attn_output))
        
        # Feed-forward with residual
        ffn_output = self.ffn(x)
        x = self.norm2(x + self.dropout2(ffn_output))
        
        return x
```

### Decoder Layer:

```python
class DecoderLayer(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, d_model, num_heads, d_ff, dropout=0.1):
        super().__init__()
        
        # Masked self-attention
        self.self_attn = MultiHeadAttention(d_model, num_heads)
        
        # Cross-attention (to encoder)
        self.cross_attn = MultiHeadAttention(d_model, num_heads)
        
        # Feed-forward network
        self.ffn = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(d_model, d_ff),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Dropout(dropout),
            nn.Linear(d_ff, d_model)
        )
        
        # Layer normalization
        self.norm1 = nn.LayerNorm(d_model)
        self.norm2 = nn.LayerNorm(d_model)
        self.norm3 = nn.LayerNorm(d_model)
        
        # Dropout
        self.dropout1 = nn.Dropout(dropout)
        self.dropout2 = nn.Dropout(dropout)
        self.dropout3 = nn.Dropout(dropout)
    
    def forward(self, x, enc_output, src_mask=None, tgt_mask=None):
        # Masked self-attention
        self_attn_output, _ = self.self_attn(x, x, x, tgt_mask)
        x = self.norm1(x + self.dropout1(self_attn_output))
        
        # Cross-attention to encoder
        cross_attn_output, _ = self.cross_attn(x, enc_output, enc_output, src_mask)
        x = self.norm2(x + self.dropout2(cross_attn_output))
        
        # Feed-forward
        ffn_output = self.ffn(x)
        x = self.norm3(x + self.dropout3(ffn_output))
        
        return x
```

sections.title: Three Transformer Variants
sections.body:
### 1. Encoder-Only (BERT-style)
```
Use: Understanding tasks
  • Text classification
  • Named Entity Recognition
  • Question Answering (extractive)
  • Sentiment analysis

Architecture:
  Input → Encoder (N layers) → Output

Examples: BERT, RoBERTa, DistilBERT
```

### 2. Decoder-Only (GPT-style)
```
Use: Generation tasks
  • Text generation
  • Language modeling
  • Creative writing
  • Code generation

Architecture:
  Input → Decoder (N layers, masked attention) → Output

Examples: GPT-2, GPT-3, GPT-4, LLaMA
```

### 3. Encoder-Decoder (Original Transformer)
```
Use: Sequence-to-sequence tasks
  • Translation
  • Summarization
  • Question Answering (generative)

Architecture:
  Input → Encoder → Decoder → Output

Examples: T5, BART, mT5, FLAN-T5
```

sections.title: Hyperparameters
sections.body:
### Original Transformer (Base):
```
d_model = 512       # Model dimension
num_heads = 8       # Attention heads
d_ff = 2048         # FFN hidden dimension
num_layers = 6      # Encoder/decoder layers
dropout = 0.1       # Dropout rate
max_seq_len = 512   # Maximum sequence length
vocab_size = 37000  # Vocabulary size
```

### Transformer (Big):
```
d_model = 1024
num_heads = 16
d_ff = 4096
num_layers = 6
```

### BERT-base:
```
d_model = 768
num_heads = 12
d_ff = 3072
num_layers = 12 (encoder only)
```

### GPT-3:
```
d_model = 12288
num_heads = 96
d_ff = 49152
num_layers = 96 (decoder only)
Parameters: 175 billion!
```

sections.title: Training Details
sections.body:
### Loss Function (Translation):
```python
# Cross-entropy loss
loss = -log P(y_i | y_<i, x)

# Teacher forcing during training:
# Use ground truth previous tokens, not predictions
```

### Optimization:
```python
# Adam optimizer with custom learning rate schedule
lr = d_model^(-0.5) × min(step^(-0.5), step × warmup_steps^(-1.5))

# Warmup for 4000 steps, then decay
```

### Regularization:
```
• Dropout (0.1)
• Label smoothing (0.1)
• Attention dropout
```

sections.title: Computational Cost
sections.body:
### Parameters:
```
Transformer-base: ~65M parameters
Transformer-big:  ~213M parameters
BERT-base:        ~110M parameters
BERT-large:       ~340M parameters
GPT-3:            ~175B parameters
```

### Memory (Attention):
```
Memory = O(batch_size × seq_len² × d_model)

Example (BERT-base):
  batch=32, seq_len=512, d_model=768
  Attention matrix per head: 32 × 512² × 12 ≈ 1GB
```

### Speed:
```
Training time (original paper):
  • Transformer-base: 12 hours (8 GPUs)
  • Transformer-big: 3.5 days (8 GPUs)

Modern LLMs (GPT-3):
  • Months on thousands of GPUs
  • Millions of dollars in compute
```

sections.title: Why Transformers Work
sections.body:
### 1. Parallel Processing
```
✓ All positions processed simultaneously
✓ vs RNN: Sequential (slow)
✓ Massive speedup on GPUs
```

### 2. Long-Range Dependencies
```
✓ Direct connections between all positions
✓ No vanishing gradients across time
✓ Can model dependencies 1000+ tokens apart
```

### 3. Flexible Architecture
```
✓ Encoder-only for understanding
✓ Decoder-only for generation
✓ Encoder-decoder for transformation
```

### 4. Scalability
```
✓ Scales to billions of parameters
✓ More data + more compute = better performance
✓ "Scaling laws" are predictable
```

sections.title: Summary
sections.body:
### Architecture Components:
```
✓ Multi-head attention (parallel heads)
✓ Feed-forward networks (position-wise)
✓ Residual connections (gradient flow)
✓ Layer normalization (training stability)
✓ Positional encoding (order information)
```

### Three Variants:
```
• Encoder-only: BERT → Understanding
• Decoder-only: GPT → Generation
• Encoder-decoder: T5 → Transformation
```

### Key Innovation:
```
Self-attention replaces recurrence
→ Parallel processing
→ Better long-range modeling
→ Scales to huge models
```
